ideas: Practical ways to close the gap

phrases.meaning: not have enough desire to act
plan targets you can actually achieve

model: I think the main reason is that our brains prefer instant gratification. Everyone knows they should eat more vegetables and exercise, but the long-term benefits feel very far away, while a bubble tea makes you happy right now. On top of that, most people are pressed for time. After a ten-hour working day, cooking a healthy meal feels like hard work, so people take the path of least resistance and order convenience food on an app. I'm guilty of this myself. I know I ought to go to the gym after work, but on busy weeks I often lack the motivation and just go home. And old habits die hard, especially if your family and friends have the same habits. Of course, some people would argue that it's simply laziness, and to some extent individuals do have to take control. But I'd say the answer is to set realistic goals. You're supposed to start small, like walking for fifteen minutes a day, rather than trying to change everything at once.
